Find the solution to the following system of equations.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{6}+\frac{5y}{6}-2=0 \\ 3x+y+6=0\end{aligned}
$$

To get rid of the fractions in the first equation, we must multiply the first equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $6.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{6}+\frac{5y}{6}-2=0 & |\,\times 6 \\ 3x+y+6=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}x+5y-12=0 \\ 3x+y+6=0\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Notice that the second equation can easily be solved for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+y+6 & =0 \\ y & =-3x-6\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $y=-3x-6$ into the first equation and then solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+5y-12 & =0 \\ x+5(-3x-6)-12 & =0 \\ x-15x-30-12 & =0 \\ -14x-42 & =0 \\ -14x & =42 \\ x & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $y,$ we substitute $x=-3$ into the equation $y=-3x-6$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-3x-6 \\  & =-3(-3)-6 \\  & =9-6 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-3,\,y=3.$
